strengths: Well-motivated practical problem addressing quadratic attention complexity and KV cache growth in long-form reasoning
Novel framing: Learning self-regulatory compression through RL rather than external heuristics or fixed schedules
Strong empirical results achieving 3× throughput improvement (5888 vs. 1483 tokens/s) while maintaining accuracy across 5 benchmarks
Interesting and well-visualized 'gap-vanishing' phenomenon showing compression ability emerges during training (Figure 3)
Clear presentation with good mathematical formulation, transparent methodology, and comprehensive baseline comparisons
Useful byproduct: Structured step summaries provide human-readable reasoning traces; human eval confirms 95% quality rate
Solid ablation study on data synthesis quality showing strict prompts significantly outperform lax prompts
weaknesses: Critical missing comparison: No direct experimental evaluation against related methods (LighterThinker, DeLeThink, other compression approaches) despite citing them
Narrow evaluation scope: Limited to mathematical reasoning only; generalization to other domains (open-ended QA, code, multi-modal) is entirely unclear

Data synthesis dependency: Relies on DeepSeek-V3.2 (external very strong model) for training data generation; raises concerns about data bias and encoding DeepSeek's reasoning patterns rather than learning generalizable compression; only 3,900 unique samples

Insufficient statistical rigor: No error bars, confidence intervals, significance testing, or standard deviations reported; human evaluation minimal (20 samples, 2 annotators); some improvements are marginal (0.1-0.2 points)

Limited mechanistic understanding: Paper demonstrates gap vanishing but provides no analysis of what information is encoded in summaries, why compression works, or how learned summaries differ from heuristic-based approaches
Incomplete ablations: No studies on key hyperparameters—summary minimum length (100 tokens), step count range (2-6), max tokens per step (6,144)—all lack justification or sensitivity analysis
Crude reward function: Binary correctness only; doesn't capture partial correctness, summary quality, readability, or efficiency tradeoffs; all steps share same reward

Reproducibility concerns: No code release mentioned; training data synthesis depends on external DeepSeek-V3.2 access; some hyperparameter choices (rope theta=40000, window size=32768) lack justification
Limited baseline diversity: Baselines are mostly variants of the proposed method; no comparison with simple prompt-based summarization, distillation, or other recent efficient reasoning approaches
Efficiency analysis gaps: Throughput reported but not per-token latency, memory consumption details, or how efficiency scales with reasoning length/difficulty

strengths: Addresses genuine practical problem: 3× throughput improvement with maintained accuracy on memory-constrained GPUs is valuable for real deployment scenarios

Novel empirical finding: Gap-Vanishing phenomenon (performance convergence of Fold to Unfold mode) is interesting and well-documented, validating that models learn effective self-compression through RL
Comprehensive experimental design: Systematic comparison of three training strategies (Unfold-RL, Fold-RL, Mix-RL) across 5 math benchmarks and 2 model scales with thoughtful ablations

Dual contribution (efficiency + interpretability): Structured step summaries enhance transparency; human evaluation shows 19/20 summaries capture critical information, providing users with readable reasoning traces
Careful data synthesis pipeline: Three-stage process with explicit quality criteria (rule-based filtering) shows attention to data quality and reproducibility
Clear presentation and visualization: Well-written with effective figures; problem formulation is clearly articulated
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: Core components (teacher rewriting, GRPO, context pruning) are borrowed or standard; main contribution is combining existing techniques in a relatively straightforward way

Insufficient mechanistic analysis of gap-vanishing: While empirical observation is valuable, explanation is shallow—lacks rigorous analysis of *why* convergence occurs, whether it represents lossless compression or adaptation to compressed contexts, or information-theoretic justification

Narrow evaluation scope: Limited to mathematical reasoning benchmarks only; generalization to other domains (QA, code, reasoning chains in NLP tasks) is undemonstrated; missing direct comparisons with LighterThinker and Delethink on identical benchmarks
Concerning scaling trend: AIME25 results show diminishing improvements (±0.0-0.2%) on harder problems, suggesting potential scalability limitations not discussed

Arbitrary data synthesis choices: Rule filters (100-token minimum, 6,144-token maximum) feel unmotivated; only 3,900 base samples is modest; heavy dependence on DeepSeek-V3.2 rewriting introduces unanalyzed distribution shift

Weak human evaluation: Only 20 samples with 2 annotators and single metric; no comparison of readability against other compression methods; no error analysis or failure mode characterization despite claimed robustness

Missing technical details: Summary length distributions not empirically measured (efficiency claims assume |s_i| ≪ |d_i| without validation); sensitivity to hyperparameters unexplored; enforcement mechanism for Fold mode during RL training unclear

Insufficient reproducibility: No project repository link (marked 'Project Repo:' with placeholder); training time/compute resources unspecified; random seeds and reproducibility scripts absent; dataset access details vague

Limited theoretical justification: No formal analysis of why trajectory-level rewards optimize token-level compression; claims of 'lossless compression' are strong but unrigorously proven; sparse binary reward signal may be suboptimal for learning compression specifically

Inconsistencies in results: Mix-RL occasionally underperforms Fold-RL (Table 1) without explanation; variance across runs not reported; evaluation metric (Pass@1 Avg@32) masks true single-attempt performance

strengths: Addresses practical efficiency problem in LLM reasoning with substantial 3× throughput improvements and 50-60% KV cache reduction
Novel self-regulatory compression perspective—enabling models to learn when/how to summarize is more elegant than heuristic-based external compression
Well-demonstrated gap-vanishing phenomenon (Figure 3) showing Fold mode converges to Unfold performance during Mix-RL training, suggesting effective learning of compression
Comprehensive experimental evaluation: 5 benchmarks, 2 model scales, proper baselines, diverse efficiency metrics (throughput, latency, peak tokens), ablation studies, and OOD generalization testing
Clear presentation with intuitive figures and well-described algorithms; Accordion format is easy to understand
Readability evaluation showing step summaries are coherent and serve as faithful substitutes for final solutions, adding practical value
Data synthesis ablation (Figure 2) systematically validates design choices (strict prompting, rule filtering)
weaknesses: Accuracy improvements are modest and lack statistical rigor: macro averages 52.8 vs 52.2 (7B), 52.1 vs 52.0 (4B) for Mix-RL vs Unfold-RL with no significance tests, confidence intervals, or error bars despite Avg@32 sampling; some benchmarks show Mix-RL underperforming Unfold-RL (AIME25: 28.3 vs 26.7)

Data synthesis pipeline raises concerns: only 3,900 samples survive filtering from 10,000 seed examples; heavy dependence on DeepSeek-V3.2 for rewriting (potential teacher bias); arbitrary thresholds (summary ≥100 tokens, K∈[2,6], L≤6,144) lack principled justification; no sensitivity analysis

Limited technical novelty: combines existing techniques (CoT + GRPO + summarization); GRPO modifications are incremental; main contribution is showing the training approach works, which is useful but not profound

Incomplete analysis of learned compression: paper claims models encode essential reasoning but doesn't explain which information is preserved/discarded, how, or why; attention heatmaps (Figure 5) show denser patterns but lack interpretation; no failure case analysis

Experimental comparison fairness concerns: Cold-Start baseline uses only SFT (expected to be weak); LightThinker/DeleThink applied to weak Cold-Start baseline rather than original settings; H2O performance (44.9%) seems suspiciously poor; limited comparison with other compression approaches

Reproducibility concerns: no project repo link in manuscript; training computational cost (GPU hours, convergence speed) not discussed; dependence on DeepSeek-V3.2 for data synthesis limits reproducibility; sparse implementation details on special token handling

Gap-vanishing phenomenon under-explained: observation is empirically clear but mechanistic understanding is superficial; hard 0/1 reward signal is crude and lacks ablation on reward design alternatives

Readability evaluation too lenient: human evaluation on only 20 samples; automated evaluation uses loose coverage criteria (Figure 9); no rigorous definition of summary faithfulness; no quality comparison across methods

Applicability constraints: maximum ~36k output length (6 steps × 6,144 tokens) may be insufficient for complex problems; method specialized for structured step-by-step reasoning with unclear generalization to other long-reasoning domains; summary length requirement may force verbose compression reducing efficiency
Missing critical analyses: no ablation on summary length threshold, sensitivity to K/L hyperparameters beyond Figure 7, comparison of sample efficiency across methods, or failure mode analysis
